idiom_name: ASP.NET Core SessionMiddleware + ISession over IDistributedCache
implementation_notes: The middleware and ISession replace the classic Session Manager: AddDistributedMemoryCache + AddSession + UseSession register a store-backed session, HttpContext.Session exposes Get/Set/Remove/Clear, and the .AspNetCore.Session cookie carries the identifier (HttpOnly true and SameSite Lax by default). The store contract is IDistributedCache, so Redis or SQL replaces the in-process cache without touching call sites. Policy stays application code: the default IdleTimeout is 20 minutes, Secure is not set by default, there is no signal when the browser closes, and the session is non-locking (the last concurrent writer wins), so logout must call Clear and cookie hardening must be configured explicitly.
pitfalls: Session state is non-locking and coherent: two requests modifying different keys can lose one another's writes, so a session is not a concurrency-safe store.
The session cookie is issued only once something is written; an empty session is not retained and a new identifier is generated for each request.
Session state is documented as ephemeral and unsupported in SignalR; keeping authoritative data there turns a cache eviction into data loss.
The in-memory provider is per-instance: without a distributed cache you need sticky sessions, which the documentation itself calls a scalability and deployment complication.
